To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a robust experiment is one that is insensitive to small changes in the subjective beliefs in models close to the analyst’s model; and 2) a model is a good model if it is robust to a set of experiments that is large and diverse.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a framework for the study of the robustness of experimental results.
we provide a formal framework that enables the analyst to test the pliability of his axioms in the presence of small subjective deviations in the beliefs of the participants.
we have formalized the concept of a robust experiment in the presence of uncertainty and we have provided conditions that guarantee the existence of such experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a theory of robust experiments is a useful tool for the design and interpretation of experiments in the context of choice under risk or uncertainty.
a robust experiment should be designed in such a way that the probability that the experiment is sensitive to a small change in the analyst's beliefs is small.
the robustness of an experiment depends on the choice of a distance between subjective beliefs and not only on the choice of an appropriate model.
